wt_petase.name: Wild-Type IsPETase
wt_petase.citation: Yoshida et al., Science 351, 1196–1199 (2016); Han et al., Nat. Commun. 8, 2106 (2017)
wt_petase.key_advantages: Natural discovery baseline; active at ambient room temperature; physiological expression.
wt_petase.key_limitations: Very low thermostability (unfolds at ~49°C); rapidly aggregates; negligible activity on crystalline post-consumer PET bottles without melting pre-treatment.

fast_petase.name: FAST-PETase
fast_petase.engineering_method: MutCompute deep learning neural network + rational selection
fast_petase.reported_degradation_metric: Almost complete depolymerization of untreated post-consumer thermoformed PET products in one week; separate tests used amorphous bottle portions and a thermally pretreated bottle at 50°C
fast_petase.degradation_substrate: 51 different post-consumer thermoformed products plus commercial bottle material
fast_petase.key_advantages: Exceptional activity on real un-pretreated post-consumer waste; robust across broad pH range (6.5–9.0); closed-loop repolymerization demonstrated.
fast_petase.key_limitations: Reported outcomes are specific to the tested substrates, pretreatment, and assay conditions; they should not be extrapolated to all post-consumer PET.

durapetase.name: DuraPETase
durapetase.engineering_method: GRAPE strategy (Greedy Accumulated Strategy for Protein Engineering)
durapetase.reported_degradation_metric: 300-fold higher degradation rate of crystalline PET film (14.8% crystallinity) at 37°C vs WT
durapetase.degradation_substrate: Commercial semi-crystalline PET film (14.8% crystallinity) & PET microplastics
durapetase.key_advantages: Drastically rigidified flexible surface loops without freezing the catalytic triad; survives high temperatures; effective on crystalline films.
durapetase.key_limitations: 10 mutations require extensive multi-site verification; requires mildly alkaline conditions (pH 9.0) for optimal activity.

thermopetase.name: ThermoPETase
thermopetase.engineering_method: Rational salt-bridge introduction & active-site cleft remodeling
thermopetase.reported_degradation_metric: 14-fold higher depolymerization product yield compared to WT at 40°C
thermopetase.key_advantages: Minimal mutation footprint (only 3 substitutions); clear mechanistic salt-bridge stabilization (Glu121-His186).
thermopetase.key_limitations: Moderate Tm increase (+8.8°C); still denatures rapidly above 55°C.

hotpetase.name: HotPETase
hotpetase.engineering_method: Computational stability consensus design + directed evolution

lcc_iccg.name: LCC-ICCG (Cutinase Reference)
lcc_iccg.engineering_method: Structure-guided rational engineering of disulfide bridges and active site (F243I/D238C/S283C/Y127G)
lcc_iccg.reported_degradation_metric: 90% depolymerization of post-consumer PET waste flakes in 10 hours at 72°C (3 mg enzyme / g PET)
lcc_iccg.key_advantages: The cited study reports depolymerization of PET flakes under specified enzyme loading and assay conditions.
lcc_iccg.key_limitations: Different enzyme family (cutinase, not IsPETase); process-scale energy demand and life-cycle impact are not assessed here.
